A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the PECs of the four low-lying states for the Cs–He pair are in good agreement with the available experimental values, whereas the results obtained for the other Cs–Rg (Rg = Ne, Ar, Xe, and Kr) pairs are in fair agreement with the experimental data.
the PECs for the Cs–Rg (Rg = Ne, Ar, Xe) pairs were improved by 1.3–3.0 cm ^{−1} compared with the results reported by Blank et al.
the PECs of all four electronic states are well characterized for Cs–Rgs, which should provide a solid basis for future theoretical studies and for the experimental investigation of these systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MRCI method, which has not been widely applied in the study of alkali–rare gas systems, is an effective method for calculating the PECs for these systems.
the PECs for the Cs–He and Cs–Ne pairs have a minimum in the Cs(6s) + Rg(1s) state, which has been overlooked in previous studies.
the PECs for the 1Σ+ and 3Σ+ states are more repulsive than previously reported, and the 1Σ+, 1Π, and 1Δ states are more attractive than previously reported.
